problem: RAG systems treat all retrieved facts as equally valid regardless of temporal provenance, producing temporal hallucination in which plausible but obsolete facts corrupt the output; semantic similarity alone may even prefer stale evidence.
method: Chronofy / Temporal-Logical Decay Architecture: Layer 1 reserves a temporal subspace in Matryoshka embeddings so fact age is structurally retained; Layer 2 integrates learnable exponential decay functions into graph-based retrieval with the decay coefficient grounded in Bayesian decision theory; Layer 3 applies Signal Temporal Logic robustness to evaluate temporal validity of retrieved knowledge and bounds output confidence by the most decayed evidence (possibilistic weakest-link).
key_assumptions: Fact age / temporal provenance is known and attachable to retrieved evidence
Exponential decay is the best-supported decay family
Older evidence is less valid (age as obsolescence)
main_contribution: A three-layer neuro-symbolic architecture that embeds temporal validity into the representation, retrieval and reasoning layers of RAG, with principled decay parameters and confidence bounding.
baselines: Five decay families compared: exponential, linear, power-law, Weibull, half-life
results: Explicit temporal decay modeling improves retrieval precision and reduces temporal hallucination; Layer 3 without temporal retrieval delivers a 37.5% precision gain but stays quiet once Layers 1-2 are active; exponential decay offers the strongest theoretical grounding with a single interpretable parameter (beta_j = 2*kappa_j), despite marginal Weibull gains on individual metrics.
limitations: Evaluation is on temporal knowledge graph forecasting (ICEWS14) and the TimE QA benchmark, not on versioned statutory/regulatory corpora
Layer 3 (STL verification) provides calibrated abstention rather than retrieval improvement and adds value only when upstream retrieval fails
Decay-family comparison was run on ICEWS14

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Chronofy operates on knowledge-graph retrieval with learned decay coefficients and neuro-symbolic logic over clinical/TKG data, not on a model-agnostic additive term re-ranking near-duplicate document versions; it equates age with loss of validity (recency-as-validity) and cites legal supersession only as motivation, whereas the proposal's core difficulty is choosing among semantically near-identical statutory versions in force at a target date.
relation_to_idea.basis: Full-text introduction and method show exponential temporal decay integrated into retrieval and explicit legal-supersession motivation ('regulatory interpretations are superseded by new rulings'), indicating partial conceptual overlap; evaluation benchmarks differ from a versioned-statute retrieval benchmark.
